pov.mode: close third, past tense — the series' established voice: the cataloguing narrator (counts things, names places precisely), diegetic documents in italics with their own plain first-person register (the Power Log), emotion through procedure and objects, dry oblique dialogue, PG-13, no modern idiom.
knowledge_boundary: Cael is eighteen; nine + anomaly; party FIVE (Oryn is north on her route; 'Thornwater in nine days'). Injuries: Cael's ribs and calf still knitting on their own (taped, improving; he can walk and work); everyone else mended.

The party knows: stillhounds hunt declarations; shale-backs flee them; 'quiet ground' as a rumor (Chapter 4: 'everybody knows... nobody goes in'). In THIS chapter Pike gives the folklore in full for the first time — everything a carter knows and nothing a researcher does: quiet ground is where the sigil goes to sleep; a handful of places along the void roads; carters walk around them; stillhounds live in them; nobody knows why and nobody has needed to because the rule is don't go in; he has walked past the Fallow Ring two hundred times and never stepped over the line; 'Thirty years on the roads and I've never met a practitioner who did it twice.' Asked what the line is: 'You'll know. Your Arbiter tells you. It stops.' NOTHING beyond that: no perimeter measurement, no fused stone, no survey stakes, no 'the Quieting' (Karis has not coined it), no theory.

The contract: a broker's posting, well priced, for recovery of 'surveyor's instruments abandoned at a site on the Fallow road' with a map reference that is quiet ground. Seln notices the contract's LANGUAGE is registry prose ('abandoned at a site') under a Lowmarch broker's seal — 'somebody wrote this who learned to write inside' — and says so; nobody knows more. Teague's crew turned the contract down (Pike says so unasked).

Teague does not appear in conversation. Oryn does not appear; the council notes the Fallow road runs through Thornwater on the ninth day — the day she said — and nobody says 'bring her'; Karis writes it down.
No letters, no Vastin, no watchers.

purpose: Part 1's closing chapter: the book's freedom at full height (the ledger moved on the traverse, hold contracts beginning to come to them) and the contract that ends it — the recovery posting whose map reference makes Pike go still, the folklore of quiet ground given whole and institutional by the man who keeps the only honest record out here, a five-voice council that takes the job anyway, and the Part's summary log entry.

scene_shape.opening_state: Back at Lowmarch from Oxhollow. Pike's ledger entry for the traverse (mapped, delivered, cart lost, crew intact — he gives them the map and charges them the cart; Cael accepts it as fair). The unit's standing now real: hold contracts beginning to come to them instead of only to Teague's crew.
scene_shape.pov_goal: Take the first artifact-recovery posting they qualify for — and understand why the best crew on the board would not.
scene_shape.opposition: Pike's stillness at the map reference; the folklore's one rule (don't go in); a contract written in the wrong prose; and Karis, who would go alone if they didn't.
scene_shape.turn: The posting: a broker's contract, well priced, for recovery of 'surveyor's instruments abandoned at a site on the Fallow road', map reference given. Pike reads it and goes still. He tells them what he knows — the folklore whole (see knowledge_boundary), ending with 'Your Arbiter tells you. It stops.' Karis's underlined rumor has just become a location.
scene_shape.choice: The council at Lowmarch's inn, five voices: it pays BECAUSE nobody will take it; Teague's crew turned it down; the instruments are worth the contract; the site is two days east. Seln finds the first wrong thing — registry prose under a broker's seal — and it goes in the log without being understood. The route runs through Thornwater on the ninth day, the day the healer said; nobody says bring her; Karis writes it down. They take it: because it pays, because the freedom chapter taught them they can, and because Karis would go alone.
scene_shape.outcome: Contract taken; two days east through Thornwater; Part 1 closes with the freedom intact and the first crack in it (the prose, the stillness, the rule).
scene_shape.closing_state: The chapter ENDS ON THE LOG, Part 1's summary entry: 'Eight weeks. Seven contracts. Pike says there's ground out here where the Arbiter goes quiet, and nobody goes in twice. Karis has been waiting her whole life for a sentence like that. Seln says the contract was written by someone from inside. I say it pays. Two days east, through Thornwater, on the day the healer said. For eight weeks nothing out here has read me. I'd like to see what a place that reads nothing does with that.'

must_include: Pike's traverse entry (map delivered, cart charged) and Cael accepting it as fair; the standing shift (hold contracts coming to them) shown through the board, not asserted.
The recovery posting as an object (broker's seal, the phrase 'surveyor's instruments abandoned at a site on the Fallow road', a map reference).

Pike's stillness and the folklore given whole, in his register, with the three verbatim beats: 'I've walked past the Fallow Ring two hundred times. Never once stepped over the line. Thirty years on the roads and I've never met a practitioner who did it twice.'; Karis: 'What's the line?'; Pike: 'You'll know. Your Arbiter tells you. It stops.'

Seln's finding on the contract's language (registry prose under a broker's seal; 'somebody wrote this who learned to write inside') — logged, not understood; Pike saying unasked that Teague's crew turned it down.
The five-voice council with each voice in register; the Thornwater/ninth-day observation; nobody says 'bring her'; Karis writes it down; the decision taken for the three stated reasons.
The chapter ENDS on the Part 1 summary log entry as given (the previous chapter ended on an image).
Cael's cataloguing outside the log (the board's new postings; Pike's face going still; the map).
Manuscript format: H1 '# Chapter 8 — Quiet Ground', prose only, '---' breaks, ends on the last line of prose.
plants: Quiet ground as folklore-with-teeth (the sigil sleeps; carters walk around; stillhounds live in it; nobody goes in twice) — Chapter 9–10 measure it.
Registry prose under a broker's seal — the Compact's first reach on paper (Chapter 12, 16, 17).
'The Fallow Ring' as Pike's name for the place (descriptive site name).
Thornwater on the ninth day — Oryn joins the walk in Chapter 9.
payoffs: Chapter 4's rumor becomes a location and a contract.
Chapter 5's freedom (paid to catalogue) ends on the first job Cael takes for a reason other than pay.
prohibited_outcomes: Nobody goes to the site in this chapter; nobody measures, theorizes, or names 'the Quieting'; no fused stone, stakes, or ruin described beyond Pike's folklore.
No Oryn on the page; no Teague dialogue; no fight; no fragment use; no letters; no Vastin.
No new named people or places beyond 'the Fallow road' / 'the Fallow Ring' as Pike's terms.
The chapter does not end on dialogue or an image.
No modern idiom; no feeling/growth declarations; tic caps; no metadata.
Do not use the phrase 'at the pitch' (or 'at that pitch') — it is at the book's cap already (10 uses in Chapters 1–4). Vary attribution registers with other means.

allowed: Lowmarch in late summer (the meadow turning over, the board's new postings, the inn's council table); Pike's manner and one-armed economy; the posting's paper and seal as objects; the map.
Dialogue in established voices beyond the mandated lines; Seln's finding in his flat register.
Cael's interior cataloguing and the log.
approval_required: Any new named entity; any fact about quiet ground beyond Pike's folklore; any fact about the broker or the poster.
forbidden: Entering or seeing the site; measuring; theory; Oryn; fights; fragment use; a dialogue or image ending; metadata.
